A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assembly of the potyvirus capsid in E. coli is a complex process that requires multiple copies of the coat protein and a specific sequence in the coat protein.
the assembly of potyvirus particles requires a highly ordered structure in the core region, and the charged residues R194, D238 and E239 are important components of this structure.
the assembly of the coat protein in vitro can be divided into two distinct steps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assembly process of potyviruses is a very complex and multistep process that requires multiple amino acid residues to be in the right place at the right time.
the E. coli expression and assembly system can be used to identify the key amino acid residue(s) required for the assembly of potyvirus particles.
the coat protein can be used as a model to study the assembly process of potyviruses.
